newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat rises contrary to Chicago trend.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat rises contrary to Chicago trend.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose in trading on Friday to counter Chicago's overnight fall.
March 1997 sold 22 contracts, rising by A$1.00 to A$168.00 a tonne on the trade. Settlement prices for nearer-term contracts also rose, by about A$1.50 a tonne.

After two days when SFE wheat failed to post any trades, the March 1997 purchases were by commercial interests who may be taking a punt on Monday's pool price revision, Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said.
The futures market remained a function of the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) pool price, he said.
Falling U.S. wheat prices could bring the pool price back a little but the weaker Australian dollar was enormously in the favour of the AWB, he said.
Exactly how much the AWB was helped by the currency fall would depend on its currency hedge position, he said.

A further decline in the U.S. market to beneath US$3.70 a bushel for March would strengthen the prospect of the AWB not increasing the pool price further. But if the AWB had no hedge position in the Australian dollar it could increase the pool price slightly, he said.
That would be contrary to world wheat price trends and ultimately the AWB had to sell the wheat, he said.
Canada, with the "entire arsenal" of its record crop remaining to be sold, remained an overlooked factor in world wheat markets, he added.
